 Rodriguez left searching for answers after Mountaineers endure most lopsided loss of season
 By Greg Carey   November 16, 2026 - 3:31 pm 
 Nov 14, 2026; Morgantown, West Virginia, USA; West Virginia Mountaineers head coach Rich Rodriguez looks on the from sideline during the third quarter against the Kansas Jayhawks at Milan Puskar Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ben Queen-Imagn Images 
 MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia is assured of a losing record within Big 12 Conference play for the eighth time in 15 seasons since joining the league after a disappointing showing Saturday in a 37-14 home loss to Kansas.
 Things don’t get any easier for the Mountaineers down the stretch as they will welcome No. 21 Houston at 1 p.m. Saturday for the home finale before traveling to Utah, one of two remaining unbeaten Power Conference programs at this point.
 WVU (5-5, 2-5 Big 12) needs another win to become bowl eligible, and that accomplishment has eluded the Mountaineers in the last two games since they won at TCU, 24-20, ahead of their lone bye week.
 “A lot is riding. Every game is for a bowl game,” WVU head coach Rich Rodriguez said. “We have two really talented, ranked teams that we have to play. This is our seniors’ last home game. It’s always something to me that’s really special.   
 “For 24 hours, we should be miserable and we’re going to look at corrections, look at what the heck happened and try to fix it. Next Saturday, I don’t know if you can play much worse, but we sure as heck have to play a whole lot better and give our fans something to cheer about. We didn’t do that. We got behind from the jump, and we have our loyal fans there and didn’t give them anything to cheer for. That bothers me that we have such a great fan base and we don’t give them something to cheer for when they come out in the cold weather wanting to see us play well.”
 For the first time this season, the Mountaineers were unable to produce much of anything in the way of offense.   
 After the first of two WVU touchdowns, the Jayhawks forced the home team to punt on seven consecutive possessions.
 KU stuffed one of college football’s top rushing attacks and held the Mountaineers to 35 yards on the ground.   
 Before Saturday, WVU had rushed for no fewer than 134 yards in any game and at least 186 yards in eight of its nine contests.
 That this showing occurred in the first game this season for WVU without Amare “Bubba” Grayson after the right guard suffered an injury a week earlier against Texas Tech indicates n offensive lineman who will be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season was missed.
 “Bubba is kind of a calming presence, but it’s just one guy,” Rodriguez said. “I had some concerns because they’re pretty good up front, but my gosh. I don’t want to say panic set in, but there was probably some of that happening, which is a little bit unforeseen, because we’d played nine games up to this point. We have work to do to fix it.”
 It marked a season-low point total for WVU and the team’s most lopsided defeat this season. It was also the Mountaineers’ third home loss of the year to a Big 12 opponent, all of which have had a margin of at least 17 points.
 For a team whose defense ranks last in the league and near-last nationally in several important statistical categories, suffice it to say there is no formula for success when scoring on two of 12 possessions.
 “We didn’t block at all up front,” Rodriguez said. “I knew their front was good, but it was bad from the start in everything — pass protection, the run game was awful. I’ll have a better grasp of some of the whys after I watch the film, but there is certainly no shortage of things we have to do to get better. I think our players are pretty conscientious, but the staff failed our players and failed our program tonight.”
